value.first: Weeks 1-2: stop the short-order cooking, but keep the pressure off. At each meal put out one thing she reliably eats (the pasta or crackers) alongside one small helping of the family food, no bargaining, no "three more bites." She decides how much. Expect her to ignore the new food entirely at first and mostly eat the pasta. That is normal and it is fine.
value.second: Weeks 3-4: bring her into the food before it hits the plate. Let her pour, stir, tear lettuce, and put items on plates at 52 months she loves these small jobs. Serve new foods next to a familiar one, tiny portions, and eat the same thing yourself so she sees it. It can take 10 to 15 no-pressure exposures before a preschooler tastes something new, so keep re-offering without comment.
value.third: By week 6 you're looking for her touching, licking, or trying a bite of one new thing, not a cleared plate that's the win at this age. Keep meals to about 20-30 minutes and structured snacks in between so she comes hungry. If she's dropping foods rather than adding them, gagging on textures, or losing weight, that's worth raising with your doctor.
